M1a.description: Fold keeps a line-end hyphen before a capital, then lowercases, so a second fold joins the word.
M1a.counterexample: fold('R- M') = 'r- m', but fold('r- m') = 'rm'
M1a.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from a documented rule but is not itself documented. The rule: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'a word broken by a hyphen at a line end -> joined ... when a lowercase letter follows', and the code comment above it, 'only before a lowercase letter, so a line ending "-" before a capital or a digit stays'.
M1a.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): over the cached runs of all 35 systems we had, on all 16,288 tests each, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1a.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1b.description: Fold keeps a dash at a line end and writes it as '-', so a second fold reads it as a line-end hyphen and joins the word.
M1b.counterexample: fold('y— t') = 'y- t', but fold('y- t') = 'yt'
M1b.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from a documented rule but is not itself documented. The rule: the code comment on `_LINE_HYPHEN` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'Not a dash, which can end a line before a lowercase word', and the fold docstring's typography step, 'dash ... families unified', which writes the kept dash as '-'.
M1b.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): over the cached runs of all 35 systems we had, on all 16,288 tests each, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1b.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1c.description: Fold turns the elision '[...]' into '[ ]', so a second fold reads it as an unchecked box.
M1c.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once, so no verdict can change. The second-fold outcome follows from the order of fold's documented steps but is not itself documented. The steps: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py runs 'checkboxes' ('[ ]' -> ☐) before 'leaders' (runs of 3+ dots -> a space), so the '[ ]' that '[...]' leaves is not read as a box until a second fold.
M1c.effect_basis: The scorer folds each string once. Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): over the cached runs of all 35 systems we had, on all 16,288 tests each, no already-folded string was folded again, and making fold skip such strings changed no verdict
M1c.who_is_affected: no one today: only a second fold would read these strings differently

M1d.description: Fold reads TeX's doubled quotes ('' and ’’) as a double quote before it unifies the quote family. So a mixed pair ('’) folds to two single quotes, and a second fold reads those as a double quote.
M1d.counterexample: fold("'’") = "''", but fold("''") = '"'. So a text test for '' fails on a page that writes '’
M1d.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing. The outcome follows from the order of fold's documented steps but is not itself documented. The steps: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py turns 'TeX quotes' into '"' just before NFKC, and unifies the quote family later, under 'typography'.
M1d.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. No real text string folds differently twice this way, so only a page that writes another spelling of a gold's two quotes is affected
M1d.who_is_affected: a text test whose gold writes two single quotes ('') against a page that writes a mixed pair ('’), or the reverse

M1e.description: Fold removes a bullet only where it starts a line, so in '• •' it removes the first and keeps the second. The second then starts the text, and a second fold removes it too.
M1e.why_this_status: No doc promises that folding twice changes nothing, and the scorer folds each string once. The rule: the fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py, 'a bullet glyph starting a line -> a space'; docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold, case fold-bullet) shows a bullet inside a line kept.
M1e.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The scorer folds each string once, and no real text string folds differently twice this way
M1e.who_is_affected: no one seen: only a second fold reads these strings differently

M2e.description: Fold reads the case of the letter after a line-end hyphen, so the upper and lower case of the same words can fold differently.
M2e.counterexample: fold('RE- M') = 're- m', but fold('re- m') = 'rem'
M2e.why_this_status: The fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py joins a line-end hyphen only 'when a lowercase letter follows'; docs/scoring/order.md (case ord-case-hyphen) shows 'R- M' not found in 'r- m'.
M2e.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The 18 real tests it touches are listed, so it can change their verdicts
M2e.how_common: 18 real tests: those with a line-end hyphen that fail on their answer in another case
M2e.who_is_affected: a page that writes such a line in another case than the gold (for example a heading in capitals) fails the test

M2g.description: Fold makes ideographic full stops ASCII only after its leader rule, so a run of them is kept as '...', not read as a leader.
M2g.counterexample: fold('Name 。。。 5') = 'name ... 5', not 'name 5'. A text test for 'Name 5' fails on that page and passes on 'Name ... 5'
M2g.why_this_status: docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold) reads 'runs of 3 or more dots' as leaders, and makes full-width punctuation ASCII after the leader step ('。' becomes '.', case fold-cjk). No doc says whether '。' counts as a dot for leaders.
M2g.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M2g.how_common: no real text string holds a run of 3 ideographic full stops (counted when the dataset is set); pages not measured
M2g.who_is_affected: Chinese and Japanese pages whose tables of contents or forms draw leaders with '。'

M6c.description: A '_' at the end of a paragraph joins a blank in the next one as a leader run only when markdown writes the paragraphs, so markdown and HTML can disagree.
M6c.counterexample: The same two paragraphs, 'lorem _' and then '• ____', pass the test for 'lorem _' written as HTML and fail it written as markdown. Markdown separates the paragraphs with a newline, so the bullet starts a line and fold removes it; the '_' then joins '____' into one leader run, which fold drops. HTML separates them with a block break only, so the bullet is kept and stops the run.
M6c.why_this_status: The scorer does this on purpose: the comment on `BREAK` in omni_parse_bench/views.py says a block break is 'no line start to a pattern anchored on "\n" (a bullet opening a block is not a bullet opening a line)'. The leader rule (`_LEADERS` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py) allows white space (`\s*`) inside a run, so a run crosses a block break or a newline (M22). The bullet only stops it in HTML, where it is kept. No doc says markdown and HTML may then differ.
M6c.effect_basis: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): over all 35 systems we had, on all 16,288 tests each, making fold's bullet rule treat a block break as a line start too gave 0 pass-to-fail and 0 fail-to-pass in every test kind; it changes the folded text of 374 pages, which hold 1,591 tests
M6c.how_common: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): a bullet opens a block right after a block break on 3,261 of about 102,800 pages (35 systems x 2,937 pages; 16,089 bullets), counted with a pattern match
M6c.who_is_affected: markdown and HTML outputs of the same paragraphs, when one opens with a bullet glyph next to a run of '_'; either format can be the one penalised

M7c.description: A `<sup>` mark right before a number joins it.
M7c.counterexample:
`

11,240.00

` reads '11,240.00', so the number test for 1,240.00 fails
M7c.why_this_status: views.html promises only that a superscript never joins what it follows (the comment on `_SUP` in omni_parse_bench/views.py; docs/scoring/internals.md, The text view, rule 6). No doc covers a mark before a number.
M7c.effect_basis: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): making `</sup>` a space too changed 0 verdicts; 105 digit joins on 31 pages, none on a page with a number test
M7c.how_common: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): 105 joins on 31 pages
M7c.who_is_affected: a page that puts a superscript mark right before a number fails that number's test

M7e.description: A superscript mark inside a phrase reads as a spaced number, so a text test for the phrase fails. A bracketed marker there is ignored (M7d).
M7e.counterexample:
Text('Probiotic strains') fails on `

Probiotic1 strains

`, which reads 'probiotic 1 strains'. It passes on `

Probiotic[1] strains

`
M7e.why_this_status: docs/scoring/present-text.md shows a `<sup>` marker ignored at the end of the text (case text-sup-marker), and a superscript read as a digit (case text-exponent). No doc says whether a mark inside a phrase is a marker or a digit. The present retry that drops markers (`unmarked` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py) takes bracketed markers only.
M7e.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M7e.who_is_affected: a text test whose gold spans a word that the page marks with a footnote set as a superscript

M10e.description: A `\(..\)` span between two stray dollars is read as math by the text tests but not found by the equation test.
M10e.counterexample: A page writes a price, an equation in `\(..\)`, and another dollar on one line: `$5.00 \(a_2\)&$`. The text tests read `a_2` as math. The equation test pairs the two dollars into one span, `5.00 \(a_2\)&`, which renders to nothing, so a test for the equation `a_2` fails although the page writes it.
M10e.why_this_status: docs/scoring/present-latex.md lists `\(..\)` as a math span; here the equation test keeps only the dollar pair around it, `5.00 \(a_2\)&`, which renders to no symbols, so the span is lost.
M10e.effect_basis: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): over all 35 systems we had, on all 16,288 tests (3,268 equation tests), no page has a stray-dollar pair around a `\(..\)` span that renders to nothing, no equation test's gold sits in such a span, and a fix changed 0 verdicts
M10e.how_common: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): 0 of about 102,800 pages (35 systems x 2,937 pages)
M10e.who_is_affected: equation tests on pages that mix prices and `\(..\)` math on one line

M11b.description: Only present accepts a hyphenated word broken after its hyphen. Order, repeat and table_cell fold 'aa- bb' to 'aabb', whether the page or the gold holds the break.
M11b.counterexample:
Order('aa-bb', 'tail') fails on `

aa-
bb

tail

`. The reverse also fails: Order('self- aware', 'tail') on `

self-aware

tail

`, while present passes both
M11b.why_this_status: The label covers the direction this relation tests: a page that breaks the word. The docstring of omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/hyphenation.py says 'Only text presence uses this fallback', and docs/scoring/internals.md (The hyphen rule, cases hyph-order, hyph-repeat, hyph-cell) shows those three tests failing. The reverse direction, a gold that holds the broken word ('self- aware') against a page that writes 'self-aware', also passes present and fails the other three. It follows from fold joining a line-end hyphen in every string, the gold's included (docs/scoring/internals.md, The hyphen rule). It is an artefact in the gold, not a verdict the docs promise.
M11b.effect_basis: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): extending the hyphen fallback to order, repeat and table_cell would change the verdict of 9 tests, all from fail to pass. Both directions occur. In 8 of the 9 the gold holds the broken word: a correct page failed because of an artefact in the gold. The record does not describe the ninth. It does not say whether 9 is for one system or summed over the 35 systems
M11b.how_common: Measured by the authors on cached runs of the released suite (not included here, so not re-runnable from this package): 9 of the 16,288 tests (for one system or summed over the 35 systems: not recorded)
M11b.who_is_affected: a page that breaks a hyphenated word after its hyphen fails order, repeat and table_cell tests of that word (present accepts it); and a correct page fails those tests when the gold holds the broken word

M12c.description: A number gold of '0', one ',' and three digits is read as a decimal (0,250 as 0.250). The docs read one ',' and three digits as a thousands mark.
M12c.counterexample:
Number('0,250') fails on `

0250

` and passes on `

0.250

`; Number('1,250') passes on `

1250

`
M12c.why_this_status: docs/scoring/present-number.md reads 'one `,` and three digits: a thousands mark' (case gold-comma-three), and so does the docstring of `number` in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py. The code makes an exception for a whole part of '0' that no doc names, and it changes which pages pass. The label says what the docs say: 0.250 is the likelier meaning, so the docs may be what needs the fix.
M12c.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. One real number test has such a gold
M12c.how_common: 1 of the 323 real number tests: num_tables_derived_768745cf_p5_6, gold '0,237),' (counted when the dataset is set)
M12c.who_is_affected: a number test whose gold is 0, a comma and three digits: a page that writes the digits without the comma fails, and one that writes 0.237 passes

M15b.description: Fold lowercases and does not casefold, so a letter whose upper case lowers to other letters is lost.
M15b.why_this_status: The fold docstring in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py says 'lowercased'; docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold, case fold-case: 'no letter is changed into others') shows 'STRASSE' and 'straße' folding apart.
M15b.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. The 15 real tests it touches are listed, so it can change their verdicts
M15b.how_common: 15 real tests: 12 in polytonic Greek, 2 with dotless ı, 1 with ß
M15b.who_is_affected: a page that writes such a word in upper case fails a test whose gold is in lower case

M16.description: When two blocks with the same box hold a place, the first listed decides the verdict.
M16.counterexample: a text test passes on blocks [text, heading] with one box and fails on [heading, text]
M16.why_this_status: docs/scoring/layout_kind.md: the holder is the smallest covering block, 'on equal areas, the first listed' (case lay-tie); `holder` in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py takes `min()` over the blocks, which keeps the first of equal areas.
M16.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M16.how_common: not measured: counting it needs system outputs (their blocks), which this package does not hold
M16.who_is_affected: an output listing two blocks with one box and different labels: their order decides

M22.description: A paragraph break joins what is on either side of it in two ways, so an added paragraph can fail a text test that passed alone. A leader run can span the break, so a text that ends in one '_' fails once the next paragraph holds only more '_'. And a line-end hyphen joins across the break, so a text that ends in a hyphen fails once the next paragraph starts with a lowercase letter.
M22.counterexample:
Text('a _') passes on `

a _

` and fails on `

a _

__

`: the three '_' make one leader run across the break, and fold reads the page as 'a'. Text('well-') passes on `

well-

` and fails on `

well-

known

`: fold reads the page as 'wellknown'
M22.why_this_status: No doc says whether a leader run or a line-end hyphen stops at a block break. docs/scoring/internals.md (Fold) says runs of 3 or more '_' become a space, and that a line-end hyphen before a lowercase letter is joined. `_LEADERS` and `_LINE_HYPHEN` in omni_parse_bench/normalize.py allow white space (`\s*`, `\s+`) after the run or the hyphen, and the text view's block break reads as white space. The leader case holds for dots, dashes, '=' and '*' too.
M22.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M22.who_is_affected: a page whose text test starts or ends with one '_', '.', '-', '=' or '*' next to a paragraph that adds two more (such as a blank in a form); and a text test that ends in a hyphen, before a paragraph that starts with a lowercase letter

M23a.description: Present forgives inserted letters, and some deleted ones: j letters inserted into the text, or deleted from a page that holds only the text, or deleted at the text's end, can pass with a budget below j. Two more forms: a text that starts or ends the page text gets about 1.5 times its budget for substituted letters, and a letter moved a few places costs one edit.
M23a.counterexample: Text('lorem ipsum dolor sit amet', k) passes on 'lorem izpsum dolqor sit amjet' (3 letters inserted) from k = 2, and on 'lorem ipsum dolor sit' (5 characters deleted at the end) from k = 3. Text('lorem ipsum', 2) passes on 'abc xxxem ipsum' (the text ends the page, its first 3 letters substituted) and fails on 'abc xxxem ipsum dolor'. Text('abcdefgh', 1) passes on 'zz acdebfgh zz' (b moved 3 places: edit distance 2)
M23a.why_this_status: The scorer's docs promise a budget of edits: docs/scoring/present-text.md says present allows 'up to `max_diffs` character edits'; in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py the `_ratio` docstring says it 'passes when the best partial match is within `max_diffs` edits', and the comment on `EPS` says 'rapidfuzz returns exactly that ratio for k edits'. That holds for substituted letters (M3), not for inserted ones: rapidfuzz's partial ratio scores an inserted letter as less than one edit. docs/scoring/internals.md (The edit budget) now states the inserted and deleted letters measured here. It names swapped letters too, but not a text at the edge of the page text, nor a moved letter.
M23a.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. It can only turn a fail into a pass: no page within its budget failed in these checks. A test with max_diffs 0 is not affected: its threshold is an exact match
M23a.who_is_affected: text tests with max_diffs 1 or more: a page that adds letters inside the text, drops letters at its end, misreads letters where the text starts or ends the page text, or moves a letter, can pass with more edits than the test allows

M23b.description: Table_cell compares whole cells by a ratio over both lengths, so an inserted or deleted letter costs about half an edit: j such letters can pass with a budget below j.
M23b.counterexample: TableCell('lorem ipsum dolor sit amet', k) passes on the cell 'lorem izpsum dolzor sit amzet' (3 letters inserted) from k = 2
M23b.why_this_status: docs/scoring/internals.md (The edit budget) says table_cell 'compares whole cells with a ratio over both lengths, so an inserted character costs half an edit', and docs/scoring/table_cell.md lists it as a blind spot (case cell-insertions: the output is wrong but passes). A deleted letter costs about half an edit by the same ratio; the docs say so in words for insertions only.
M23b.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. It can only turn a fail into a pass: no cell within its budget failed in these checks
M23b.who_is_affected: table_cell tests with max_diffs 1 or more: a cell with extra or missing letters can pass with more edits than the test allows

M25b.description: With more edits allowed, order can fail a page it passed. The squeezed retry runs only when an item is missing, and a match that spends edits can hide the start that passed. Since every exact copy is kept, two items written exactly keep passing (M25a).
M25b.counterexample:
Order('aa', 'a ba') passes on `

b b a ab ab

` with max_diffs 0 (the squeezed text 'bbaabab' holds 'aa' before 'aba') and fails with max_diffs 1
M25b.why_this_status: docs/scoring/order.md says both items are searched again in the squeezed text only 'If either is missing', and that the test passes when any match of `before` starts before any match of `after`. It does not say where a match that spends edits starts. No doc says a larger budget can fail a page.
M25b.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with. It needs max_diffs 1 or more
M25b.who_is_affected: order tests with max_diffs 1 or more whose items overlap or repeat on the page, or are found only with spaces removed

M26.description: Two blocks of equal area hold a place in list order only when their float areas are equal. Rounding can make the second listed the smaller, and it then holds the place.
M26.counterexample: A heading block [0.2, 0.8, 0.4, 0.9] and a text block [0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 1.0] both have area 0.02. Their float areas are 0.019999999999999997 and 0.01999999999999999, so the text block holds the place [0.2, 0.8, 0.3, 0.9] and a heading test there fails
M26.why_this_status: docs/scoring/layout_kind.md says the holder is the smallest covering block, 'on equal areas, the first listed' (case lay-tie). `holder` in omni_parse_bench/scorers/unit_tests/runners.py compares the float areas exactly.
M26.effect_basis: not measured: the authors did not re-score the cached runs for it, and this package holds no system outputs to measure it with
M26.how_common: not measured: counting it needs system outputs (their blocks), which this package does not hold
M26.who_is_affected: an output with two blocks of equal area but different shapes and labels over one place
